requirement: An imported copy keeps Akeeba's output folder, answers an http visit with one hop to https, and is built without the wizard tab open

oracle.ref: PR #1655 (fix); fix evidence: Prod QA 23/10/2026: a Joomla 4.4 copy with Akeeba Backup 9.9 showed 'Output directory unwritable' (#1650); an http visit to a copy looped 301 to itself (#1651, measured on dev: the container answered 301 https, tracy-web passed it on as 301 http); closing the wizard tab while files were packed left the run at done/handing_over with no copy until the recovery link was opened (#1652).
oracle.invariant: 0 failures. #1650: a copy whose webroot has Akeeba Backup gets its output folder back, empty but for a deny-all .htaccess and index.html, at import (provision.sh own_webroot, before the chown) and after a Sync from live apply; a site without Akeeba, a folder already there, or a symlink anywhere on the path (`administrator`, `administrator/components`, the component folder) is left alone, and the owner step gives away nothing outside the webroot; the folder stays out of the webroot history. #1651: an http visit to a copy whose CMS forces https gets one 301 to https on the same host and then 200, never a 301 back to http; a stand on an explicit port still gets the Location on its own scheme and port. #1652: a finished read is handed over by the host itself, once, with the owner's session, with no tab open; a lane restart between done and the handover sends it at the next boot; a refusal is written on the run and not retried. #1652: the wizard waits for a pending host handover and follows the host's job without filing one; a tab reopened mid-build follows the host's job; a host that never answers, refuses, or is absent leaves the wizard to hand over itself; a TAKEN met while the host's request is in flight ends on the host's job, one build. #1652: a TAKEN met after the wait while the host handover is still pending is the host building: the wizard keeps following it, shows no failure, and asks again itself only once the host gives it up.
oracle.productSourcesScope: file-level: the files the case imports, reads or runs (declaration line, or the first code line); the invariant is exercised through them, the executed assertion is the case command
